context noun

the words around a passage

also contexts, in context, out of context, from the context

classical

Cic. Part. 82: in tōtō quasi contextū ōrātiōnis
Quint. 11.2.28: verbōrum (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. circumstance: context (verbōrum contextus)

contextus, contextūs m.

noun, fourth declension

the connection, the run of a text; context

A joining together: the coherence of a speech or a system (Cic. Fin. 5.83), the run of the words (very frequent in Quintilian). Cicero softens it with quasi. It is not the circumstances of an event, which Latin calls rēs or tempora.

Other words

  • superior et īnferior scrīptūra — what is written before and after (a passage)

    phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Inv. 2.117

    Cicero’s way of saying that the context settles an ambiguous word.

Examples

  • deinde ex superiōre et ex īnferiōre scrīptūrā docendum id, quod quaerātur, fierī perspicuum.

    next, one must show from what is written before and after that the point in question becomes clear.Cic. Inv. 2.117

  • sed in tōtō quasi contextū ōrātiōnis haec erunt inlūstranda maximē

    but in the whole fabric, so to speak, of the speech these points will have to be brought out most of allCic. Part. 82

See also text, phrase, word.
